long_biography.plain_text:
At Microsoft, Gabe Newell spent 13 years across systems, applications and advanced technology, including programme management for the first two Windows releases. He left to co-found Valve with Mike Harrington. Half-Life made the young studio a success, then Steam changed its economics by building a direct digital-distribution platform for games from Valve and other developers.

Valve remained private as it expanded into further games, hardware and Steam, leaving Newell with a large ownership stake in the company he started. He later co-founded Starfish Neuroscience, a flat, self-directed team developing minimally invasive ways to interact with the brain and body. The venture aims to move experimental neurotechnology from the laboratory towards practical clinical use.
